diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $\fA\in\R^{\stateDim\times\stateDim}$ in~\eqref{eqn:generic:GLE} is Hurwitz and $\|\lyapOper^{-1}\gleOper\|_2<1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The advertised guarantee is for the GLE introduced under only the stated Hurwitz assumption, whereas the certification theorem additionally assumes a strict fixed-point contraction. The proposed scaling changes the matrices \(N_j\) and hence changes the GLE solution; preservation of its column space does not provide a norm approximation to the original \(X\). Thus scaling cannot remove the missing regime from the claimed solution guarantee.

failure_location.quote: Our first contribution is the derivation of efficient computable error estimates such that, for any prescribed user tolerance $\tol$, the computed approximation $\tilde{{\fX}}$ of $\fX$, where $\fX$ is the exact solution of \eqref{eqn:generic:GLE}, satisfies $\|\fX-\tilde{\fX}\|_2\le\tol$; see \Cref{teo1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict all approximation guarantees to GLEs satisfying the contraction hypothesis, or develop a certified method for the original unscaled equation when that hypothesis fails.
issues.overall_effect: The paper does not establish certified approximation of every GLE in its advertised scope, only of equations satisfying an additional contraction condition.
issues.title: Unqualified certification claim omits the contraction hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The source supports only a substantial restriction of the advertised problem class; retaining the broad claim would require a different convergence and certification argument.

issues.failure_explanation: For a general Hurwitz matrix, the smallest singular value of the Lyapunov operator is not twice the smallest singular value of \(A\). For example, for \(A=-\varepsilon I+\omega J\), where \(J\) is the real skew-symmetric rotation matrix, \(A\) is Hurwitz and \(\sigma_{\min}(A)=\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+\omega^2}\), while \(\mathcal L\operatorname{vec}(I)=\operatorname{vec}(-2\varepsilon I)\), so \(\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal L)\le 2\varepsilon\). The stated denominator can therefore underestimate the error arbitrarily.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the denominator by a valid lower bound for the separation of the Lyapunov operator and supply an efficient certified way to compute that bound; then propagate it through the GLE estimate and scaling discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The certified Lyapunov error estimate, the residual contributions in the main GLE estimate, and the computable bound used to estimate the contraction factor are not valid for the stated class of Hurwitz matrices.
issues.title: False singular-value identity invalidates the Lyapunov residual bound
issues.why_classification: The direct repair requires estimating a large Lyapunov operator rather than merely \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\), undermining the central inexpensive certification and scaling claims unless a new certified bound is developed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\fX_k = \fZ_k\fZ_k^\T$ is the unique solution of the Lyapunov equation~\eqref{alg:statIterGLE:lyap} in iteration $k$ of \Cref{alg:statIterGLE}.

issues.failure_explanation: In the implemented algorithm, the right-hand side at iteration \(k\) is formed from the approximate factor \(\tilde Z_{k-1}\). The exact solution of that inner Lyapunov equation therefore depends on \(\tilde X_{k-1}\), not on the exact outer iterate \(X_{k-1}\). Consequently the recurrence used in Proposition 2 and its a posteriori difference bound do not apply to the sequence introduced in Theorem 1. Inner-solve errors propagate through subsequent outer right-hand sides, but the proof accounts only for the two current residuals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide an inexact fixed-point error analysis that includes propagation of all inner residuals, and replace the theorem's estimator and stopping rule accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Even after correcting the Lyapunov-operator constant, the stated stopping criterion does not certify the output of the actual inexact stationary algorithm.
issues.title: The inexact outer iteration is treated as the exact fixed-point iteration
issues.why_classification: A contraction-based perturbation analysis may preserve a comparable guarantee, but it requires a new nontrivial lemma and a modified estimator rather than a local algebraic edit.

issues.failure_explanation: Dissipativity implies \(w^TA_j^Tw=w^T\operatorname{sym}(A_j)w\le-\alpha_j\|w\|^2\), where \(\alpha_j=-\lambda_{\max}(\operatorname{sym}A_j)>0\). It does not imply the bound with \(\sigma_{\min}(A_j)\). For \(A=-I+\omega J\), the quadratic form equals \(-\|w\|^2\) while \(\sigma_{\min}(A)=\sqrt{1+\omega^2}\), so the proof claims arbitrarily more damping than exists and the prescribed perturbation can be insufficient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \(\sigma_{\min}(A_j)\) by the actual dissipativity margin \(-\lambda_{\max}((A_j+A_j^T)/2)\) in the perturbation condition and propagate the revised constant.
issues.overall_effect: The perturbed approximate Gramian is not guaranteed to satisfy the LMI, so the ensuing stability and balanced-truncation certification based on this construction are unreliable.
issues.title: The perturbation size in Theorem 4 uses the wrong dissipativity constant
issues.why_classification: A short local replacement by the correct coercivity constant preserves the theorem's dissipative-matrix regime and qualitative guarantee, although it may produce a larger perturbation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As already discussed in \Cref{sec:MORexplained}, the fact that each subsystem mode is stable is not sufficient to conclude that the \SLS is stable for each $\switch\in \calS$.
Moreover, if the solution of the \LMI is not successful, it is possible to exploit the fact that the asymptotic stability of the \SLS can still be guaranteed under a minimum switching time condition

issues.failure_explanation: The paper establishes at most a claim that individual reduced modes are stable. It explicitly acknowledges that this does not imply stability under arbitrary allowed switching and instead proposes an a posteriori common-Lyapunov LMI test or an additional minimum-dwell-time condition. Neither condition is imposed by the PBR construction, so the stated unconditional switched-ROM stability guarantee is not established.

failure_location.quote: To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel \MOR strategy for \SLS that guarantees the stability of the \ROM and provides a generalized error bound without requiring the \LMIs to hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the unconditional stability guarantee and state only modewise stability, or add and enforce a common-Lyapunov or dwell-time condition sufficient for switched stability.
issues.overall_effect: A central advertised benefit of PBR—stability of the resulting switched reduced system for the allowed switching class—is unsupported.
issues.title: The PBR construction does not guarantee stability of the switched ROM
issues.why_classification: The least source-supported repair materially weakens the guarantee from stability of the switched ROM to modewise stability or excludes arbitrary switching.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, each $\tilde \fA_j$ is, by construction, stable due to the stability properties of classical square root balance truncation.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrices used are generalized, possibly singular Gramians, and the displayed relation is only semidefinite. The proposition assumes neither positive definiteness/minimality nor a strict Lyapunov inequality for the retained block. Classical square-root balanced-truncation stability therefore cannot simply be invoked, and the construction itself may be undefined when the balanced singular values to be inverted vanish. Exact solvability of the GLEs alone does not supply these missing hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Then, each subsystem of the switched system $\switchedSysRedJumps $ defined in \eqref{eqn:new:red:system} is stable.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add conditions ensuring that the balancing transformations are well defined and that each retained block satisfies a strict Lyapunov inequality, then supply the corresponding reduced-stability argument; otherwise weaken the conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: Even the weaker modewise stability assertion used to motivate PBR is not proved for the proposition's stated inputs.
issues.title: Modewise stability proposition lacks hypotheses ensuring strict reduced stability
issues.why_classification: Comparable modewise stability may survive under standard definiteness or minimality conditions, but the source needs additional substantive hypotheses and an actual argument.

issues.failure_explanation: When \(G_{c,o}<0\), which is exactly the case selected by \(H(-G_{c,o})\), the real square root \(G_{c,o}^{1/2}\) is undefined. Moreover, the contribution arising from \(-G_{c,o}>0\) in Lemma 5 must be added as \(\sqrt{-G_{c,o}}\), not subtracted as written. Multiplication by a Heaviside factor does not make an already undefined square root meaningful.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the correction by a properly defined nonnegative term such as \(\sqrt{\max\{-G_{c,o},0\}}\), likewise express the H-term piecewise, and redo the subadditivity step.
issues.overall_effect: The central PBR error estimator and its numerical decomposition are not real-valued as defined and therefore do not constitute a valid computable upper bound.
issues.title: Theorem 6 takes square roots of potentially negative correction terms
issues.why_classification: The intended positive-part estimate appears recoverable locally, but both the formal theorem and the implemented estimator require a substantive sign and domain correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The defining summation shadows the free index \(k\), so its right-hand side is independent of the left-hand subscript and all \(s_k\) would be the same. It also uses the undefined symbol \(\tilde n\), invokes \(s_{\tilde\stateDim+1}\), and indexes \(\tilde\sigma\) by \(s_k\) although the preceding notation defines \(\tilde\sigma_k\). Hence the chain of intermediate model dimensions needed for the iterative balanced-truncation argument is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define an ordered cumulative sequence of retained dimensions, the corresponding singular-value blocks and intermediate trajectories, fix all summation limits, and restate the iterative bound using those objects.
issues.overall_effect: The sums in the PBR error bound cannot be evaluated, and the claimed iteration of the one-step estimate is not a mathematically specified argument.
issues.title: The intermediate dimensions in Theorem 6 are undefined
issues.why_classification: Repair requires reconstructing the indexing and intermediate-model construction, but it can plausibly be contained within the theorem without changing the overall proof architecture.
